solution: During the interval X the trace falls, so the air pressure inside the lungs is dropping below the pressure of the outside air, and that is what pulls air in — this is inhalation. Inhalation happens because the diaphragm contracts and flattens downward while the external intercostal muscles contract to lift the ribs up and out, so the chest cavity and the lungs get bigger and the pressure inside falls. Ribs moving downward and inward, relaxation of the external intercostals and a decrease in lung volume all belong to exhalation, and each of them would push the pressure up, not down.

Aerobic respiration begins in the cytoplasm, where one six-carbon glucose molecule is split into two three-carbon pyruvate molecules and a small amount of energy is released — so the first two blanks are pyruvate and energy. This pyruvate is then broken down further inside the mitochondria in the presence of oxygen, and the final products are carbon dioxide, water and a much larger amount of energy. Options that place carbon dioxide in the cytoplasm step, or make oxygen a product instead of a requirement, reverse the order of the pathway.

Epithelial cells are packed tightly against one another with almost no intercellular space and only a very thin cementing material between them — that close packing is exactly what allows epithelium to act as a continuous protective covering and lining, so the statement that epithelial tissue has intercellular spaces is the wrong one. The other three statements are correct: the matrix of a connective tissue does vary with its job (fluid in blood, hard and rigid in bone, tough in cartilage), fat is indeed stored as adipose tissue below the skin and between internal organs, and striated (skeletal) muscle fibres really are long, cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate.
notes: The four statements are printed as 1-4 in the stem but the options refer to them as (A)-(D); I have read them positionally, so statement 3 (epithelial tissue has intercellular spaces) is '(C)'. That reading is the only one that makes the option set sensible.

solution: Tendons join muscle to bone and must not stretch, so they are made of tough, inelastic white collagen fibres. Ligaments join bone to bone across a joint and must give a little as the joint moves, so they are rich in elastic yellow fibres. Cartilage has its own cells called chondrocytes sitting in spaces in a solid but flexible matrix, while bone has cells called osteocytes embedded in a hard matrix of calcium and phosphorus salts.

A nerve cell always carries its message in one direction. The dendrites pick up the stimulus and start the electrical impulse, which travels into the cell body, then along the axon, and finally reaches the axon terminals, where chemicals are released across the synapse to the next cell. Any sequence that starts at the cell body or the axon terminal, or that skips the cell body, reverses this one-way path.

Auxin is the plant hormone that makes cells elongate behind the growing tip and that stimulates roots to form on a cutting, so cell enlargement and root formation are both genuine auxin functions. Inducing dormancy is not an auxin job at all — that is done by abscisic acid, the stress and growth-inhibiting hormone. Auxin also does the opposite of overcoming apical dominance: auxin made at the shoot tip is what suppresses the side buds, and it is cytokinin that releases them. So the two items that are not auxin functions are the one about inducing dormancy and the one about overcoming apical dominance.
notes: Statement 4 is garbled: 'secreted by the posterior lobe' refers to the posterior pituitary, an animal endocrine gland, and has nothing to do with a plant hormone. Read as 'overcome apical dominance' it is still not an auxin function (auxin causes apical dominance; cytokinin overcomes it), so the answer is unaffected. As in the other match-style item, statements are numbered 1-4 while the options name them A-D, so I read them positionally.

solution: Phenotype means the traits you can actually see or measure in an organism, such as flower colour or plant height. Genotype is the set of genes the organism carries for those traits, whether or not they show up. A dominant factor is one that expresses its effect even when only one copy is present, while a recessive factor stays hidden and cannot express its effect unless both copies are recessive.

An inherited feature such as the ability to roll the tongue is carried by genes, and genes are stretches of DNA. Inside a non-dividing nucleus that DNA is present as a loose tangle of fine threads called chromatin, which condenses into chromosomes when the cell divides — that thread network is the labelled part in the diagram. The dense round body inside the nucleus is the nucleolus, which makes ribosome parts, and the boundary with its pores is the nuclear envelope that controls what enters and leaves; neither of these stores hereditary information.
notes: The leader lines for the two upper labels are very close together in this low-resolution crop. I have taken the upper one as pointing to the nucleolus / upper envelope and the lower one as pointing into the chromatin threads, which is how the labels are described and is the only reading under which the question has a correct answer. If in the printed original the two leaders are the other way round, the answer would become the other upper label.

solution: Insecticides kill insects, so the flies and the caterpillars — the primary consumers that feed on the trees — will fall sharply in number. Every animal higher up this web depends on them: frogs and sparrows eat the insects, and snakes and hawks eat the frogs and sparrows, so the loss passes up the chain and the top predators drop too. The frogs and sparrows cannot increase when their own food is being destroyed, and there is nothing in the web to suggest caterpillars would be hit harder than flies since the same spray reaches both.

The Amoeba in the drawing still has a single undivided body, but its nucleus has stretched out into a long dumb-bell shape across the cell — this is the nuclear division stage of binary fission, before the cell itself pinches into two. The yeast cell beside it carries a small outgrowth with its own nucleus already inside, which is a completed bud, so yeast has reproduced by budding. Calling the Amoeba stage cytokinesis is wrong because the cytoplasm has not begun to split, and the descriptions that give budding to Amoeba or binary fission to yeast swap the two organisms' methods.
